claim_text: Structural growth in hyperscale/cloud data-centre demand underpinned the stated thesis of continued footprint expansion.
counterfactual: Without sustained hyperscale/cloud demand growth the stated 'continue expanding CyrusOne's footprint' thesis loses its basis and a ~25% premium to the unaffected price could not be underwritten; the bid would be materially re-priced or not made.
factual_basis: S08 pre-signing leasing (20 MW / $37.8m signed in Q3 2021; 82% of space under development pre-leased); S09 independent report that the sector boomed during COVID-19 and funds bought DC assets to capitalise on demand; S01 buyer statement on expansion opportunities.
rival: PR-08 capital-liquidity regime (cheap 2021 capital) as the operative driver; VM-15 valuation arbitrage independent of demand.
discriminating_test: PROPOSED: obtain DEFM14A management projections and bidder materials; demand-driven thesis predicts price justified by growth capex/lease-up assumptions, liquidity-driven thesis predicts price justified by entry multiple vs private marks with modest growth.

claim_text: 2021 capital-market liquidity for infrastructure and real-estate funds enabled a wave of data-centre take-privates (Blackstone/QTS agreed June 2021; this deal; American Tower/CoreSite same week).

rival: PR-01 demand growth as sole root cause.

claim_text: KKR/GIP acquire CyrusOne to earn returns above hurdle by owning and funding the continued expansion of a scaled hyperscale platform with long-term private capital, independent of any strategic combination.
counterfactual: If the consortium could not earn a hurdle return by funding CyrusOne's development with long-term private capital, there is no strategic combination to support $90.50 cash and the consortium bid would not have been made at this price.
factual_basis: S01 joint KKR/GIP statement: 'continue expanding CyrusOne's footprint ... leveraging our global resources, access to long term capital and deep expertise to support the Company's growth'. No operating combination named.
rival: BM-06.2 contracted cash-flow acquisition (yield thesis); VM-15 arbitrage-only thesis; BO-05 deployment pressure.
discriminating_test: R37: BM-23 non-terminal; paired with VM-14.1 (E1 lever) and PG-01 (E2). Discriminating test between growth-funding and yield theses PROPOSED (post-close capex vs distributions).
test_passed: R37 CONDITIONAL PASS (lever E1 via index excerpt only)
value_lever: Private long-term capital funding development pipeline (VM-14.1)

claim_text: Stated ownership lever: consortium's 'access to long term capital' to support growth, i.e. funding CyrusOne's development pipeline under private ownership rather than via listed-REIT equity and debt markets. The 'cheaper than prior owner' element is NOT evidenced.
counterfactual: Remove the capital-provision lever and the growth rationale collapses to a valuation/yield thesis; the premium would have to be justified by arbitrage alone and would be materially lower.
factual_basis: S01 stated lever; S03 target disclosed financing risk in light of capital expenditure requirements (boilerplate-grade).
rival: VM-15 public/private arbitrage; VM-14.4 duration-matched capital; VM-13 capital structure.

value_lever: Long-term private capital for development capex
